claims.text: Configurational disorder governs the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Phase transformations govern the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
Defect formation governs the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
The interplay among configurational disorder, phase transformations, and defect formation is dynamic.
High-temperature in-situ TEM can directly reveal configurational disorder, phase transformations, and defect formation in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Grain growth influences the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Defect formation influences the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Phase transformations influence the structural and chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Understanding these dynamic processes will enable optimization of high-entropy nanoalloys for high-temperature applications.
The prediction is intended to apply at temperatures above 1000°C under environments such as vacuum or inert gas.
The exact relationships among composition, microstructure, and properties under high-temperature conditions are not fully understood.
